learning_objective: 🎯 Examine how groups influence individual behavior, group dynamics, conformity, compliance, obedience, and the causes of intergroup conflict!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A group is a collection of two or more interacting people who share common goals and norms. Groups can be Primary (family, close friends - intimate) or Secondary (school class, office - formal), and In-groups vs. Out-groups ('we' vs. 'they').

main_concepts.concept_title: ⚡ Influence of Group on Individual Behaviour
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Groups change how we act. Social Facilitation means performance improves in the presence of others. Conversely, Social Loafing occurs when individuals exert less effort working collectively in a group than alone.

Social influence manifests in three ways: Conformity (adjusting behavior to fit group norms, famously studied by Asch), Compliance (doing what someone asks, e.g., foot-in-the-door technique), and Obedience (following direct commands from an authority figure, famously studied by Milgram).

Group Polarization happens when a group's initial views become more extreme after discussion. Intergroup conflicts (like prejudice or competition) arise from perceived scarcity of resources, leading to hostility that requires resolution strategies like superordinate goals.

fun_activity.title: 😴 The Social Loafing Experiment
fun_activity.instructions: Think of a group project you did in school. Did everyone pull equal weight, or did some members lean back while others did the work? Relate this real-life experience to the psychological concept of 'Social Loafing'.

exam_tips: 📌 Differentiate clearly between Social Facilitation (improved performance with others) and Social Loafing (reduced effort in group tasks).
📌 Solomon Asch's experiment on Conformity and Stanley Milgram's experiment on Obedience are critical concepts frequently asked in board exams.
📌 Know the difference between Conformity (yielding to group pressure without direct command) and Obedience (responding to direct authority).
quick_recap: ⭐ Groups provide identity and shape individual behavior through norms and roles.
⭐ Social influence can lead to positive conformity or extreme outcomes like group polarization.
⭐ Classic experiments by Asch and Milgram highlight how powerfully authority and peer pressure drive human behavior.
